---
title: "Inspecting a network"
description: >
  Where points snap to the streets, the street and transit networks as sf,
  the dates with service, and the errors in the GTFS feeds.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("setup.R")
```

Before routing, it helps to look at the network: whether the points reach
the streets, which streets each mode may use, where the stops are, on which
dates services run and what is wrong with the feeds. This page uses the
São Paulo sample that ships with the package.

```{r network}
library(peabiru)
data_path <- system.file("extdata/spo", package = "peabiru")
network <- build_network(data_path, n_threads = 2)
network
```

## Where points snap

Routing starts and ends at the nearest point of a street the mode may use,
looked for within 300 m and then within `radius`. `find_snap()` shows where
that is, and how far:

```{r snap}
points <- read.csv(file.path(data_path, "spo_points.csv"))
snap <- find_snap(network, points, mode = "CAR")
head(snap)
summary(snap$distance)
```

A point that does not snap (`found = FALSE`) is not routed and has no rows
in the results.

## The street network

`street_network_bbox()` gives the extent of the street network, and
`street_network_to_sf()` its vertices and edges as `sf`, with the modes each
edge allows, the car speed and the level of traffic stress for cyclists:

```{r streets, eval = requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)}
street_network_bbox(network, output = "vector")
streets <- street_network_to_sf(network)
head(streets$edges[, c("edge_index", "osm_id", "street_class", "length",
                       "walk", "car", "car_speed", "bicycle", "bicycle_lts")])
table(streets$edges$bicycle_lts)
```

```{r lts-map, eval = requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE), fig.alt = "The streets of the sample, coloured by the level of traffic stress for cyclists, from 1 to 4."}
plot(streets$edges["bicycle_lts"], main = NULL, key.pos = 1)
```

## The transit network

`transit_network_to_sf()` gives the stops (with whether each is linked to
the street network) and one line per trip pattern of each route:

```{r transit, eval = requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)}
transit <- transit_network_to_sf(network)
head(transit$stops)
head(sf::st_drop_geometry(transit$routes))
```

## Dates with service

Public transport is only routed on dates when services run.
`check_transit_availability()` counts the services active on each date:
without dates, every date with service; with `dates`, or `start_date` and
`end_date`, those dates.

```{r dates}
check_transit_availability(network, start_date = "2019-05-11",
                           end_date = "2019-05-14")
```

## GTFS errors

`get_gtfs_errors()` lists the errors the 'GTFS' library of R5 (gtfs-lib)
finds in the feeds. This feed has a few of priority `"MEDIUM"`
(duplicated keys), which do not stop a network from being built:

```{r errors}
get_gtfs_errors(network)
```

Errors of priority `"HIGH"` do: a feed whose trips refer to a route that
does not exist, for instance. Here is a copy of the sample feed with one
such trip.

```{r broken}
broken <- file.path(tempdir(), "spo_broken")
gtfs <- file.path(tempdir(), "spo_gtfs")
dir.create(broken, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(gtfs, showWarnings = FALSE)
invisible(file.copy(file.path(data_path, "spo_osm.pbf"), broken))
unzip(file.path(data_path, "spo_gtfs.zip"), exdir = gtfs)
trips <- read.csv(file.path(gtfs, "trips.txt"), colClasses = "character")
trips$route_id[1] <- "NO_SUCH_ROUTE"
write.csv(trips, file.path(gtfs, "trips.txt"), row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
old <- setwd(gtfs)
utils::zip(file.path(broken, "spo_gtfs.zip"), list.files(), flags = "-q")
setwd(old)
```

`build_network()` refuses it, and `get_gtfs_errors()` takes the directory
(there is no network to pass) and lists the errors:

```{r refuse, error = TRUE}
build_network(broken, n_threads = 2)
errors <- get_gtfs_errors(broken)
errors[errors$priority == "HIGH", ]
```

Nothing is written to the data directory: the errors are found again from
the feeds each time.
